title: Notion MCP Server
summary: Connect your agent to Notion's hosted MCP server to search workspace pages, read databases and write notes, specs and tasks back.
description: Notion runs its own MCP server, so an agent can search your workspace, read a spec or a meeting page, query a database and create or update pages. It is a good fit when requirements or runbooks already live in Notion and you want them in the same chat as the code.

Setup is a URL and a browser sign-in. The agent only sees what your Notion account can see in the workspace you pick. Business and Enterprise workspaces can also use a token created by a workspace owner.
useWhen: Read the product spec before you start a feature
Write release notes into a Notion page when a release ships
Turn a task database into a list of tickets to work on
Save a design decision as a page the team can find later

mcp.name: notion
access: Reads pages and databases your Notion account can open
Creates and edits pages and comments in the workspace you authorize

example.prompt: Find the "Billing retries" spec in Notion and list the open questions at the bottom of it.
example.result: Found "Billing retries spec" in Engineering Specs. Three open questions: max retry count, whether to email on the final failure, and how to treat expired cards.

faq.question: How does it sign in?
faq.answer: The first use opens a Notion browser page where you choose the workspace and approve access. No token goes into the config.

faq.question: Can it edit every page?
faq.answer: It acts as you, so it can change what you can change. Share only the pages you are comfortable with, or use a limited account.

faq.question: Is the older /sse address still needed?
faq.answer: No. Notion says the SSE endpoint retires in February 2027. This setup uses the streamable HTTP address.

access: Reads and writes Notion content as the signed-in user
